question_text: Calculate the number of atoms contained in a cylinder $1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ in diameter by $1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ deep of (a) magnesium and (b) lead. Give your answer as a tuple: (number_of_atoms_magnesium, number_of_atoms_lead).
response:
## Solution

The cylinder has diameter $d = 1\,\mu\text{m}$ and depth $h = 1\,\mu\text{m}$.

**Volume of the cylinder:**
$$V = \pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 h = \pi(0.5\,\mu\text{m})^2(1\,\mu\text{m}) = 7.854\times10^{-13}\,\text{cm}^3$$

**Number of atoms** (using $N = \dfrac{\rho V}{A}N_A$, with $N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$):

Parameters taken from a single consistent source (Callister, *Materials Science and Engineering: An Introduction*, Appendix tables):

| Material | $\rho$ (g/cm³) | $A$ (g/mol) | Source |
|----------|---------------|-------------|--------|
| Mg | 1.738 | 24.31 | Callister App. |
| Pb | 11.35 | 207.2 | Callister App. |

**(a) Magnesium:**
$$N_{\text{Mg}} = \frac{(1.738)(7.854\times10^{-13})}{24.31}(6.022\times10^{23}) \approx 3.38\times10^{10}$$

**(b) Lead:**
$$N_{\text{Pb}} = \frac{(11.35)(7.854\times10^{-13})}{207.2}(6.022\times10^{23}) \approx 2.59\times10^{10}$$

Both materials' parameters come from the same data source (Callister appendix), satisfying the consistent-source requirement. Results are reported to 3 significant figures, matching the precision of the tabulated densities/atomic weights.

$$\boxed{(3.38\times10^{10},\ 2.59\times10^{10})}$$
